title: Example of a Training Program Plan
summary:
This chapter gives an indicative, trimester-by-trimester plan for three profiles: sedentary, active and athlete women. Programs should be customized by initial fitness, trimester and any symptoms or contraindications. Design principles include individualization, safe progression (increasing volume, not intensity), variety, body education, professional supervision and effort monitoring at 40%-60% of reserve heart rate and Borg RPE 12-14.

The trimesters have distinct goals: adapting and building a routine in the first, consolidating strength and function in the second, and maintaining mobility, posture and preparing for childbirth in the third. Tables give weekly content, frequency and intensity for each profile, followed by common components for endurance, strength, core, flexibility and pelvic floor.
points: Weekly frequency is three times for sedentary, four to five for active and five to six for athlete women.
Session duration is 20-30 min (sedentary), 30-40 min (active) and 45-60 min (athlete).
Intensity is RPE 11-12 (sedentary), RPE 12-13 (active) and RPE 13-15, no impact (athlete).
Weekly volume is 90-120 min (sedentary), 150-180 min (active) and 200-250 min (athlete); these figures are indicative and can be modified if a greater load is safely handled.
The first trimester is weeks 0-13, the second 14-27 and the third 28-40.
Sedentary women start with light walking 10-20 minutes three times per week at RPE 10-11 in weeks 1-4, reaching 30 minutes walking plus 10 minutes core and pelvic floor at RPE 12 by weeks 9-13.
Athletes keep 60%-70% of usual volume in weeks 1-4 and reduce to 70% of prepregnancy volume in weeks 14-18.
Third-trimester intensity drops, for example RPE 10-12 in weeks 37-40 for active women and athletes.
Common components: endurance 20-45 minutes three to five times per week, and strength of 6-8 exercises, 2-3 sets, 10-15 repetitions.
takeaways: Pick your profile (sedentary, active, athlete) and follow its frequency and duration ranges as a guide.
Increase volume gradually rather than intensity.
Use the Borg scale (RPE 12-14) and talk test to self-regulate effort.
Replace impact with options like elliptical or water aerobics as pregnancy progresses.
Include core and stability moves such as bridge, bird-dog and cat-cow, plus daily Kegel exercises.
Prioritize technical control over workload and take regular hydration breaks.
cautions: Avoid prolonged supine positioning from the second trimester onward.
Avoid anaerobic peaks, high-impact and jumping exercises, and the Valsalva maneuver, as noted in the plan tables.
